newsitem.title: FINLAND: LIPPONEN WANTS UNIONS, EMPLOYERS TO PREPARE FOR EMU.
newsitem.headline: LIPPONEN WANTS UNIONS, EMPLOYERS TO PREPARE FOR EMU.

text.p: Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said on Thursday that trade unions and employer confederations should prepare for Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) conditions.
"The government expects that the labour market organisations together prepare for EMU conditions," Lipponen told a briefing for journalists.
"From that basis the government is ready to discuss measures to strengthen the economy required by EMU," he said.
Lipponen said the close cooperation between his five-party left-right-green coalition and the labour market organisations should continue.

"As prime minister, I will do everything in my power so that the broad cooperation may continue. Otherwise Finland will not survive in the global competition and in the European Union, whether we are in the first group in EMU or not," he said.
The government will give in spring an EMU report to parliament, Lipponen said.
"The government will keep the opposition up to date on the EMU preparations and will try to reach as broad-based agreements as possible in parliament," he said.
